offline.banner: Offline check: the AI analysis could not run, so this verdict comes from Tumar.AI's built-in rules only. It is less complete than a full check.

explain.inconclusive: There is too little text for the rules to judge, and the AI check could not run.
explain.low: The offline rules found no known scam pattern. Without the AI check this is not a clean bill of health, so stay careful.
explain.moderate: The offline rules found weak warning signs, such as pressure or talk of money, but no strong scam signal. Treat it with caution.
explain.high: The offline rules found a strong scam signal, such as a request for a one-time code, login details or a lookalike link.
explain.critical: The offline rules found several strong, independent scam signals.

contribute.title: Help improve scam detection (optional)

contribute.preview_title: This is exactly what would be stored:
contribute.preview_note: Phone numbers, card numbers, email addresses and one-time codes have been removed. Links are kept, because they are what identifies the scam.

image.title: Screenshot Scanner
image.subtitle: Upload a screenshot — a message, a page, a receipt, a QR code — and get an evidence-based risk report.
image.allow_external_help: With this on, the image and the text read from it may be sent to a configured AI provider for a second opinion. With it off, everything runs on this server.
image.privacy_note: The image is validated, read and discarded. It is never stored and never added to our detection corpus — only the text read out of it can be contributed, and only if you choose to.
image.disabled_by_user: External AI providers are switched off. The scan runs locally: text recognition, QR codes, link checks, scam patterns and risk scoring.
image.no_provider: No vision model is configured, so visual analysis is skipped. Text recognition, QR codes, link checks and the text model still run.
image.upload_help: PNG, JPG or WEBP, up to {mb} MB. The format is checked from the file itself, not its name.
image.too_large: That image is larger than 6 MB. Try a screenshot of just the part that matters.
image.unsupported: That file type is not supported. Use PNG, JPG or WEBP.
image.method_note: Image {size} · analysed in {ms} ms · text language: {lang}. The verdict was reached by Tumar.AI's own engine from the evidence listed above.
image.empty_text: Upload a screenshot above and your trust report will appear here.
image.local_only: No external AI provider is configured on this installation. The scan runs entirely here: text recognition, QR codes, link checks, scam patterns and risk scoring.
image.ocr_hint_missing: Text recognition (Tesseract) is not installed on this server, so text inside images cannot be read locally. QR codes and link checks still work; a vision model, if allowed, can still transcribe the text.
image.reputation_note: Link checks are local heuristics. No reputation service was consulted and no link was opened.
image.limitations_text: A low risk level means no suspicious indicator was identified by the stages that ran — not that the image is guaranteed safe. Text recognition can misread small, blurred or stylised text; a logo is not proof of who sent a message; links are judged by their address only.

explain.inconclusive: Nothing legible could be read from this image and no QR code was found, so there is no basis for a verdict. Try a clearer or larger screenshot.
explain.low: The stages that ran found no suspicious indicator: no look-alike link, no request for a code or password, no pressure wording. That is good news, not a guarantee.
explain.moderate: Some weak signals were found — wording or links that also appear in ordinary messages. Take a careful look before acting on anything in this image.
explain.high: At least one strong indicator of a scam was found — a deceptive link, a request to reveal a code, or wording aimed at tricking an automated reader. Treat this as a likely scam.
explain.critical: Several strong, independent indicators of a scam were found. Do not act on anything in this image.

rec.general: Verify through the organisation's official app or website, never through a link or number from the image.
rec.inconclusive: Upload a sharper screenshot that includes the whole message, including any links or sender details.
rec.phishing: Do not open the link. Type the official address yourself or use the official app.
rec.financial_fraud: Do not transfer money or pay any fee to receive a payment, prize or refund.
rec.credential_theft: Never enter a password or login details on a page reached from this message.
rec.identity_impersonation: Contact the organisation through its official channel to confirm the message is theirs.
rec.delivery_scam: Check the parcel on the carrier's official site using your own tracking number — carriers do not collect customs fees by chat link.
rec.investment_scam: Guaranteed returns do not exist. Check the company with the financial regulator before sending anything.
rec.social_engineering: Pause. Pressure and deadlines are the tactic — call the person or organisation back on a number you already trust.
rec.otp_harvesting: Never tell anyone a one-time code, not even someone claiming to be your bank.
rec.fake_payment_request: Confirm any payment request directly in your banking app, not from this screen.
rec.suspicious_authentication: If you did not start this sign-in, decline it and change your password from the official app.

conf.qr_exact: A QR code was decoded exactly, so the link it points to is certain.
conf.ocr_read: Text was read by OCR; small or blurred characters can be misread.
conf.vision_read: A vision model transcribed the image; its reading is not independently verified.
conf.independent_signals: Several independent signals point the same way.
conf.absence: No indicator found is weaker evidence than an indicator found, so confidence is capped.
conf.nothing_read: Nothing could be read from the image, so there is little to be confident about.

confidence.agreement: Higher confidence: our scanner and the AI agree independently.
confidence.ai_only: Lower confidence: the AI flagged this, but our scanner found no known pattern.
confidence.contradiction: Lower confidence: our scanner found strong signals the AI did not treat as dangerous.
confidence.advice_conflict: Lower confidence: this message reads like security advice, which is often flagged by mistake.
confidence.short_input: Lower confidence: the message is very short, so there is little to judge.
confidence.routine: Confidence reflects the AI's certainty on this message.
confidence.vision_agreement: Higher confidence: the screenshot reader and our engine reached the same conclusion independently.
confidence.vision_conflict: Lower confidence: the screenshot reader and our engine disagreed about this.
confidence.vision_unreadable: The screenshot was hard to read, so its reader's opinion was not counted.

breach.safe_tips_title: Your personal security tips for today
breach.meaning_text: Websites where this email was registered got hacked at some point, and data such as your email address — possibly along with passwords or personal details — became public. Scammers use this data for phishing and password-guessing attacks.
breach.rec_unique_passwords: Use a strong, unique password for every account.
breach.rec_password_manager: Use a password manager — it remembers strong unique passwords so you don't have to.
breach.rec_enable_mfa: Enable two-factor authentication (2FA) on your important accounts.
breach.rec_authenticator_app: Prefer an authenticator app over SMS codes for two-factor authentication.
breach.rec_recognize_phishing: Be suspicious of emails that push you to click links or open attachments urgently.
breach.rec_check_sender: Always check the sender's real address — display names are easy to fake.
breach.rec_software_updates: Install system and app updates promptly — they close the holes attackers use.
breach.rec_browser_safety: Type your bank's address yourself instead of clicking links to it from messages.
breach.rec_wifi_caution: Avoid logging into important accounts on public Wi-Fi, or use a trusted VPN.
breach.rec_recovery_settings: Review your account recovery email and phone number — outdated ones are a hidden risk.
breach.rec_account_monitoring: Turn on login alerts so you notice suspicious sign-ins immediately.
breach.rec_periodic_check: Re-check your email here every few months — new breaches surface all the time.
breach.rec_change_passwords: Change the password on every account that uses this email.
breach.rec_no_reuse: Never reuse the same password across different sites.
breach.rec_watch_phishing: Watch out for phishing emails and unexpected password-reset messages — attackers know this address exists.
breach.explanation_none: This address was not found in any known public data breach. That is good news, but not a guarantee — keep your guard up.
breach.explanation_medium: This address appears in known data breaches. Data linked to it — possibly including passwords — has been exposed.
breach.explanation_high: This address appears in several known data breaches. Treat every account that uses it as at risk.

password.title: Password Health
password.subtitle: Check whether a password already appears in public breach data.
password.privacy: **How this stays private:** your password is never sent to the breach database, and never to our AI engine. We hash it and send only the **first five characters** of that hash; the database replies with hundreds of possible matches and the comparison happens on our side. It cannot tell which password you checked. Nothing is written to disk, and the result below records no part of your password.
password.input_help: Checked against the Have I Been Pwned corpus using k-anonymity — only a five-character hash prefix is sent.
password.method_note: Checked against public breach records using k-anonymity. Strength is assessed on this server, offline.
password.empty_text: Enter a password above and your trust report will appear here. It will never show the password itself.
password.explanation_breached: This password appears in known breach data, which means attackers already have it on their lists. Its length or cleverness no longer matters — automated attacks try leaked passwords first.
password.explanation_weak: This password was not found in known breach data, but it is easy to guess. Short or predictable passwords fall to automated guessing long before anyone has to leak them.
password.explanation_clean: This password was not found in known breach data and is solidly built. That is good news, not a guarantee — it only covers breaches that have become public.
password.rec_change_now: Change this password everywhere you use it, starting with email and banking.
password.rec_unique: Give every account its own password, so one leak cannot open the rest.
password.rec_manager: Use a password manager — it remembers long unique passwords so you don't have to.
password.rec_mfa: Turn on two-factor authentication; it protects an account even when the password is known.
password.rec_lengthen: Make it longer — four unrelated words beat a short password with symbols in it.
password.rec_keep_unique: Keep it unique to one account, and re-check it here now and then.

about.title: About Tumar.AI
about.subtitle: Your personal AI companion for a safer digital life.
about.intro: **Tumar.AI** exists for one reason: everyday people — not just security experts — deserve real protection from online scams. We turn professional security checks into simple tools anyone can use.
about.why_tumar_text: A **tumar (тұмар)** is a traditional Kazakh amulet, worn to protect its owner from harm. Tumar.AI is exactly that — a digital amulet that protects ordinary people from the dangers of the online world.
about.matters_text: Most scam victims are ordinary users, not companies. The tools that could protect them exist, but they are scattered, technical, and full of jargon. Tumar.AI puts the essential checks in one friendly place and explains every result in plain language.
about.stack_table:
| Layer | Technology |
| --- | --- |
| Language | Python |
| UI framework | Streamlit |
| AI engine | Google Gemini |
about.principles_text:
- **Privacy by design** — nothing you check is written to disk: no database, no logs. Results stay in your browser session and disappear when it ends.
- **Your password stays yours** — it is never sent to the breach database or to our AI engine; only a five-character hash prefix leaves this server (see the Password Health page).
- **Honesty** — Tumar.AI is a decision aid, not a guarantee. Every verdict shows its confidence and how it was reached. When in doubt, contact your bank or service provider directly through official channels.

wifi.title: 🎓 Campus Wi-Fi Defense
wifi.text: Public university Wi-Fi is shared by thousands of devices. Never access financial accounts or internal student portals without verified HTTPS and an encrypted DNS (DoH/DoT) or VPN enabled.

passwords.title: 🔐 Master Your Credentials
passwords.text: Never reuse passwords between your university portal, social media, and email. Use an open-source password manager (like Bitwarden) with a strong, 4-word diceware passphrase.

twofa.title: 🔑 Upgrade Beyond SMS 2FA
twofa.text: SMS verification codes can be intercepted via SIM-swapping and SS7 attacks. Switch your Google, Telegram, and GitHub accounts to hardware security keys (FIDO2) or authenticator apps (Aegis/Yubico).

terminals.title: 💻 Public Terminal Hygiene
terminals.text: When using library or computer lab workstations, always browse in Incognito/Private mode, never save credentials, and explicitly click 'Sign Out' before leaving your seat.

secrets.title: ⚡ Avoid Committing Secrets
secrets.text: Student developers: never commit .env files, API tokens, or database passwords to public GitHub repositories. Use .gitignore and automated secret scanners like git-secrets.

phishing.title: 🎣 Spotting University Phishing
phishing.text: Beware of emails claiming 'Emergency Financial Aid Refund' or 'Urgent Course Tuition Payment'. Always check sender headers and never log in via emailed links.

telegram.title: 📱 Telegram Account Hardening
telegram.text: In Telegram Settings → Privacy and Security: Enable Two-Step Verification (Cloud Password) and restrict 'Who can find me by phone number' to 'My Contacts'.

encryption.title: 🔒 Full Disk Encryption
encryption.text: Enable BitLocker (Windows) or FileVault (macOS). If your laptop is lost or stolen on campus, attackers cannot pull raw files from the hard drive without your encryption key.
